examGuide.title: Mental model and derivation
examGuide.body:
Element order is the smallest positive number of repeated group operations giving the identity. In a finite group a subgroup's order divides group order. A cyclic group is Abelian and has one subgroup for each divisor of its order. In additive Z_n, order(k)=n/gcd(n,k); generators are residues coprime to n. Neither every group nor every element of a cyclic group is necessarily a generator.

**Key relationship:** ord(k in Zₙ under +) = n / gcd(n,k)

examGuide.title: A repeatable solving procedure
examGuide.body:
1. Identify identity and operation.
2. Compute modular multiples or powers.
3. Use order divisibility after verifying group assumptions.

examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: For modular additive groups, an element a is self-inverse when 2a≡0 mod n; its order is n/gcd(a,n). In a direct product, equations hold componentwise and an element’s order is the lcm of component orders. Lagrange’s theorem constrains subgroup orders but does not assert that every divisor is the order of a subgroup in an arbitrary group.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
What is the order of (2,3) in the additive group Z6×Z8?

**Answer: 24.** The order of 2 in Z6 is 6/gcd(2,6)=3. The order of 3 in Z8 is 8/gcd(3,8)=8. The tuple returns to zero after lcm(3,8)=24 additions.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
The identity in an additive group is zero. The inverse of a mod n is −a mod n, not generally its multiplicative inverse.

Integers modulo n under multiplication are not generally a group; restrict to units to obtain inverses.

examGuide.title: Worked question patterns
examGuide.body:
#### Pattern 1 · MCQ

Order of 4 in additive Z₁₂ is:

- **A.** 4
- **B.** 12
- **C.** 2
- **D.** 3

**Answer: D.** 12/gcd(12,4)=3. Three copies of 4 give zero modulo 12.

#### Pattern 2 · MSQ

Every cyclic group satisfies:

- **A.** Every cyclic group has infinitely many elements
- **B.** Every subgroup is cyclic
- **C.** Every element generates it
- **D.** It has an identity

**Answer: B, D.** Subgroups of cyclic groups are cyclic and all groups contain an identity. Finite cyclic groups exist; not every element is a generator.

#### Pattern 3 · NAT

How many generators does additive Z₁₀ have?



**Answer: 4.** The coprime residues are 1,3,7,9. Hence φ(10)=4 generators.

examGuide.title: Work through the supplied PYQs
examGuide.body:
#### GATE 2024 CS2 · Q63 · NAT

[Open the original question and try it](/#/lesson/groups?tab=practice)

**What is tested:** Groups and cyclic groups. Refer to the original image for complete givens and diagrams.

1. A tuple is its own additive inverse exactly when doubling every component gives zero in the corresponding modular group.
2. In Z2, both 0,1 qualify; in Z3 only 0 qualifies; in Z4, 0,2 qualify. These choices are independent.
3. Count=2×1×2=**4**, including the identity tuple.

#### GATE 2023 CS · Q51 · MSQ

[Open the original question and try it](/#/lesson/groups?tab=practice)

**What is tested:** Groups and cyclic groups. Refer to the original image for complete givens and diagrams.

1. Symmetric difference corresponds to XOR of membership bits, so it is closed and associative on the power set; it is also commutative.
2. The identity is ∅, since A△∅=A. Every set is its own inverse because A△A=∅. Therefore H is a group.
3. The complement is not the inverse in general: A△Aᶜ=X rather than ∅ for nonempty X. Select **A,D**.
